text:
carlos: Heads up — since the thin-batch sampler change yesterday, I'm seeing a clear 95p/99p latency tail for requests with <= 16 tokens. Spike started ~20:30 UTC.
jen: saw that in dashboards too. p50 unchanged, but p95 jumped ~230ms and p99 ~420ms on a few nodes.
priya: any change in kernel selection logs? could be flipping to a slower kernel for short sequences.
carlos: profiler output attached (snippet below). Note the kernel_choice counters; short sequences now route to slow_attention_v2 more often.
carlos: ```
# kernel_choice summary
seq_len<=32: slow_attention_v2: 62%  fast_attention_opt: 38%
seq_len>32: fast_attention_opt: 99%
``` 
sam: that 62% is new. Before the sampler tweak it was ~15%.
linus: sampler change was the "thin-batch sampling" tweak that biases queue formation to favor older requests to reduce latency for long tails. Might be creating different batch shapes.
jen: kv-cache miss rates for short requests changed? if kv hits drop we might be losing prefix cache locality and forcing different code paths.
ainey: (infra-bot) alert: increased NVLink stalls on gpu-pod-7 between 20:25-20:50 UTC (connected to thread 1911122334)
priya: carlos, can you paste a short request trace (token budgets + batch shape) for one of the p99 events?
carlos: pasted one below. note the batch shape sequence: [3, 5, 2] -> merged into microbatch with padding to 8 -> kernel selected slow_attention_v2 due to padded shape heuristic.
carlos: ```
request_id: rq_8f2
token_budget: 16
batch_elements: [3,5,2]
merged_seq_len: 8
kernel: slow_attention_v2 (reason: padded_shape_threshold)
latency: 412ms
``` 
sam: aha, padded_shape_threshold changed in the sampler config? we recently lowered the shape-stability tolerance to allow faster merges.
linus: yes, commit a3b9 changed shape_stability_tolerance from 0.25 -> 0.12 to reduce wait-time. That'll make the coalescer more aggressive, which can produce these skinny but uneven batches.
priya: hypothesis: aggressive merging + thin-batch sampler -> more padding leading to kernel heuristics picking a kernel optimized for smaller internal tiling but slower on NVLink-heavy configs. Combined with KV cache churn -> more memory traffic -> NVLink stalls.
jen: can we reproduce locally with microbench? run the harness with the new sampler config and a mix of short requests.
carlos: ran a local replay with the new sampler and saw the same kernel flip. Repro commands:
carlos: ```bash
./tools/replay --trace sample_short_reqs.json --sampler-config configs/sampler_thin.yaml --profile
``` 
sam: quick mitigation: revert the shape_stability_tolerance change and throttle the thin-batch bias. Rollout a canary to nodes 7 and 8 only.
linus: agree. I'll queue a canary rollback for those hosts and instrument kernel_choice and kv_hit_rate metrics.
priya: also add an A/B compare to measure p95/p99 and NVLink busy.
jen: action items:
- linus: rollback sampler tweak on canary nodes (infra) (ETA 15m)
- carlos: run replay with instrumented profiler and attach flame graphs (ETA 30m)
- sam: prepare a config variant with less aggressive padding (ETA 45m)
- priya: run a KV cache stress test and measure miss amplification (ETA 1h)
carlos: I'll collect a short perf record and upload. If rollback fixes p99 we should revert the change in main branch and iterate on a safer heuristic.
sam: thanks. marking as high-priority regression. pinging @oncall if rollback doesn't reduce p99 in 30m.
infra-bot: deploy job started: revert/sampler-tweak-canary -> nodes [gpu-pod-7,gpu-pod-8]. CI job id: deploy-4821.
jen: saw immediate drop on canary after revert. p95 down ~150ms, p99 down ~300ms on those two nodes.
priya: nice. keep monitoring cluster-wide for a bit before full rollback.
carlos: summary: root cause appears to be interaction between thin-batch sampler and shape_stability_tolerance change; that produced padded microbatches that trigger slower kernel selection and increased NVLink/memory pressure, which amplified p99 latency for short requests.
linus: will open a short follow-up PR with a simulation harness that verifies kernel_choice distribution before merging sampler changes.
sam: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident board with notes.
